T.title.title: Prompt Engineering
T.title.screen: AI ENGINEER ROADMAP · MODULE 5 / PROMPT ENGINEERING / Engineering Learning Circle · 26 October 2026.

O.wall.title: Four questions
O.wall.say:
A couple of years back, "prompt engineering" was everywhere. Some called it the job of the future; some called it a fad that would be dead in a year. By the end of today, you should be able to answer four questions.

[click] Why does the same AI give you a different answer every time you ask?

[click] What does a prompt that works every time actually look like?

[click] When should you show it examples, or tell it to think first?

[click] And is prompt engineering still worth learning in 2026?

[click] Let's settle that last one before we start. Scan this, or type the link, and vote. Is it a core skill, a fad, or are you not sure yet? We'll ask exactly the same question at the end, and see if anything moved.
O.wall.screen: A wall of real posts, headlines, job ads and comments about "prompt engineering" pops up in date order (2020 → 2026), the year faint behind it. Then four questions, one per click, alternating white and gold: "Why does the same AI give a different answer every time you ask?" · "What does a prompt that works every time look like?" · "When should you show it examples, or tell it to think first?" · "Is prompt engineering still worth learning in 2026?" [click] The questions clear; question 4 moves to the top; LIVE VOTE: a QR code and a short link on the left, three bars on the right (Yes, it's a core skill · No, it's a fad · Not sure yet) filling as votes arrive.
